entities.summary: Francisco Jiménez de Cisneros, OFM was a Spanish cardinal, religious figure, and statesman. Starting from humble beginnings he rose to the heights of power, becoming a religious reformer, twice regent of Spain, Cardinal, Grand Inquisitor, promoter of the Crusades in North Africa, and founder of the Alcalá University. Among his intellectual accomplishments during the Renaissance in Spain, he is best known for funding the Complutensian Polyglot Bible, the first polyglot version of the entire Bible, which was mass produced using Johannes Gutenberg's printing press.

entities.name: Francisco Jiménez de Cisneros
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Francisco Jiménez de Cisneros (1436–1517) was a Spanish Franciscan cardinal, religious reformer, statesman, and Grand Inquisitor who served twice as regent of Castile — one of the most powerful churchmen in Spanish history and a defining figure of the transition from medieval to early modern Spain.

Born into modest Castilian nobility, Cisneros entered the Franciscan order and became confessor to Queen Isabella I of Castile (1492) — a position of enormous political influence. He was appointed Archbishop of Toledo (1495), making him the primate of Spain, and then Cardinal (1507). As Grand Inquisitor (1507–1517), he oversaw the forced conversion of Muslims in Granada (1502) and the burning of Islamic manuscripts — policies of coerced religious uniformity that matched and in some ways exceeded his predecessor Torquemada's severity.

Cisneros reformed the Spanish Church with remarkable energy, requiring Franciscan friars to return to strict poverty, founding the University of Alcalá de Henares (1499), and commissioning the Complutensian Polyglot Bible (1514–1517) — the first critical edition of the entire Christian Bible, printed in four parallel columns of Greek, Latin, Aramaic, and Hebrew. He served as regent of Castile after Ferdinand II's death (1516), ruling Spain until the arrival of the young Charles I (future Holy Roman Emperor Charles V) and dying at the age of 81, still in office. He represents the union of Renaissance humanism and Counter-Reformation zeal that characterized Spanish imperialism.
